notes: Status LED chain: 8 on one GPIO, so the GPIO budget (17 of ~23-26 already used) is not a constraint. Level-shifted through a spare 74AHCT541 channel.
RGB lets history be encoded as colour on one LED rather than one LED per time window: bright red = limiting now, orange = within 5 min, dim yellow = within 10 min.
Alternative if footprint matters: WS2812C-2020 (C2976072), 2x2 mm, stock 2245.

WHY ADDRESSABLE AT ALL: eight indicators on one GPIO. Discrete SMD LEDs would need eight pins and the assignment table has none spare. The cost is the three 12 mA constant-current drivers inside each package - about twenty times the power of a plain LED at 2 mA. An I2C LED driver on the existing bus would also cost zero pins and about a twentieth of the power, at the cost of colour; not taken, but it is the alternative.

BUDGETED AT 0.12 W: eight LEDs, one colour, 25% duty. The datasheet ceiling (70% greyscale on tricolour, p.3) is 1.01 W, which would put the board 1.04x OVER its thermal capacity - but that case is a floodlight, not a status display. The cap belongs in the LED driver rather than in the display logic, because the uncapped case is one API call away.

PLAIN LEDs ARE A REAL ALTERNATIVE AND GPIO COUNT DOES NOT DECIDE IT. Eight 0805 indicators (e.g. YLED0805R, C19171391, 127k stock, 0.8 cents) on a 74HC595 sharing SCLK/MOSI with the Ethernet module need ONE latch pin - the same as this chain - and the 595 would replace the 74AHCT541, which exists only because SK6812 wants 5 V logic. That option is 0.053 W against 0.120 W and $0.15 against $0.87. It loses on part count (17 against 9, because it needs eight current-limiting resistors) and on colour, which now carries the negotiated contract: the bar reads watts across 180 W, so on a 36 W contract one LED lights whether the wall is dark or the supply is small.

RETIRED in favour of the side-emitting C2890041. The reasoning in the notes above about why the chain is addressable rather than plain LEDs, and about the brightness cap, carries over unchanged - both are properties of the family, not of this package. Note the replacement's pin order differs: DIN and VDD are swapped.
designVerdict: REJECTED - superseded twice. First by the side-emitting SK6812D-EC3210R (C2890041), then by the top-view SK6812-EC20 (C2909058), which is what is fitted. Not on the board.
